## Recommendation

On paper, the best option for these 1,000 tons is **cleaning the hulls, recovering kernels, then selling to the local dairy**. It nets about $98 per ton expected ($98,000 total). That is $13 per ton ($13,000) more than selling straight to the local dairy at $85 per ton ($85,000).

This result depends on placeholder values. The cleaning cost, the kernel value, and the 20-mile haul distance are all placeholders. Only the dairy price range and the haul rate are sourced [giannini2026]. Because the edge comes from the placeholder processing cost and kernel value, get a toll-cleaning or equipment quote before committing. If the quote is higher or kernel recovery is lower, selling straight to the local dairy is the safe fallback.

Two data gaps remain: aflatoxin is untested, and moisture and crude fiber are not entered.

## How the options compare

| Option | Expected net per ton | Expected total | vs. local dairy per ton |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean, recover kernels, sell to local dairy | $98 | $98,000 | +$13 |
| Sell to local dairy | $85 | $85,000 | baseline |
| Distant dairy | $56 | $56,000 | -$29 |
| Bioenergy | $17 | $17,000 | -$68 |
| Compost or soil | $16 | $16,000 | -$69 |
| Hull powder food ingredient | needs quote | n/a | n/a |

- **Clean and recover:** it sells at the same dairy price as the local dairy, so a dairy price change moves both equally. Its edge comes only from kernel value, minus cleaning cost.
- **Distant dairy:** the $75 per ton haul eats the premium. The buyer would need to pay $160 per ton to match the local dairy. Its $116–$146 price is a placeholder.
- **Bioenergy and compost:** all values are placeholders, and they would need $103 and $99 per ton to match the local dairy.
- **Food ingredient:** it has no price, so it is not recommended. A buyer would need to quote $175 per ton to match selling to the local dairy. There is no public market price yet [gras2026].

## What could change the answer

- **Dairy price swings.** Prices have gone from a slump of about $60 per ton to $130 per ton [farmprogress_low, wcngg2022]. That moves both dairy-based options together, so the gap between them stays tied to cleaning cost and kernel value.
- **Cleaning cost and kernel recovery.** Recovered kernels may grade lower than standard kernels. Kernel recovery is roughly 1–1.3% of hull-pile weight [abc_food2025].
- **Buyer leverage.** About 97% of hulls already go to dairy rations, so dairy buyers have leverage [farmprogress_low].
- **A real food-ingredient quote** at or above $175 per ton would put that option ahead of the local dairy.

## Quality and risk checks

- **Aflatoxin: not tested.** Test before selling for feed or food. This applies to the dairy, clean-and-recover, distant dairy, and food options.
- **Crude fiber: not entered.** Feed sales need crude fiber below 15% [wcngg2022]. Cleaned hulls must still meet that standard.
- **Moisture: not entered.** Hulls are typically delivered at 88–91% dry matter [wcngg2022].
- The clean-and-recover option also needs access to cleaning and kernel-recovery equipment.

## Assumptions and sources

**Sourced:** the dairy hull price range of $76–$106 per ton and hauling rates of $0.20–$0.40 per ton-mile [giannini2026]; the 15% crude fiber standard [wcngg2022]; price history [farmprogress_low, wcngg2022].

**Placeholder:** all haul distances, cleaning and other processing costs, kernel value, and the distant dairy, bioenergy, compost, and food prices.

- [abc_food2025] Almond Board of California, "Unlocking New Value: Commercializing Almond Hulls as Food Ingredients": https://www.almonds.org/almond-industry/industry-news/unlocking-new-value-commercializing-almond-hulls-food-ingredients
- [farmprogress_low] Farm Progress, "Almond hulls – Low prices call for expanded markets": https://www.farmprogress.com/tree-nuts/almond-hulls-low-prices-call-for-expanded-markets
- [giannini2026] UC Giannini Foundation, "Almond Shell Circularity in California's Bioeconomy" (2026): https://s.giannini.ucop.edu/uploads/pub/2026/06/26/v29n5_3_mg7Nqvg.pdf
- [gras2026] AgInfo, "Unlocking New Uses for Almond Hulls": https://www.aginfo.net/report/65481/32/Unlocking-New-Uses-for-Almond-Hulls
- [wcngg2022] WCNGG, "Almond Hull Prices are a Bright Spot" (2022): https://wcngg.com/2022/04/18/almond-hull-prices-are-a-bright-spot-for-the-almond-industry/

These are estimates. Confirm prices with buyer quotes and test hull quality before deciding.

## Recommendation

**Do not sell these hulls as feed yet, and do not pick a winner from this report.** Crude fiber is 16%, and the feed standard requires below 15% [wcngg2022]. That makes the local dairy, the cleaned-and-recovered option, and the distant dairy all ineligible as feed. Aflatoxin has not been tested, and moisture was not entered.

The only eligible priced options are bioenergy and compost or soil. Of those, **bioenergy ranks first**, at about $17 per ton expected ($17,000 for the lot). That is a weak result, and it rests entirely on placeholder prices. The next step is to test the hulls, then get real quotes.

## How the options compare

Net is per short ton, after processing and hauling, with coproduct value included. The local dairy is a reference point only, because it is ineligible.

| Option | Eligible | Expected net/ton | Expected total | Vs. local dairy/ton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bioenergy | Yes | $17 | $17,000 | -$68 |
| Compost or soil | Yes | $16 | $16,000 | -$69 |
| Clean, recover kernels, sell to dairy | No | $98 | $98,000 | +$13 |
| Local dairy (reference) | No | $85 | $85,000 | $0 |
| Distant dairy | No | $56 | $56,000 | -$29 |
| Hull powder food ingredient | Needs quote | none | none | none |

The three feed options look better on paper, but they are not open to this lot as it stands.

**Food ingredient** has no price, so it is not recommended. A buyer would need to pay about $175 per ton for it to match selling to the local dairy. Bioenergy would need about $103, compost about $99, and distant dairy about $160.

## What could change the answer

- **Cleaning the hulls.** If cleaning brought crude fiber below 15%, the feed options could become eligible. The clean-and-recover option is listed at $98 per ton against $85 for the local dairy. Its edge comes only from its own costs and recovered kernels, since its price follows the local dairy. The cleaning cost and kernel value are placeholders, and there is no evidence yet that cleaning lowers fiber enough.
- **Dairy price swings.** Hull prices have ranged from a slump of about $60 per ton to $130 per ton [farmprogress_low, wcngg2022]. About 97% of hulls go to dairy rations, so buyers have leverage [farmprogress_low].
- **Real quotes.** Bioenergy and compost prices are placeholders, so real quotes could move them a lot.
- **Distance.** Distant dairy hauling is $75 per ton, which can erase the premium.

## Quality and risk checks

- **Crude fiber:** 16% fails the 15% feed standard [wcngg2022].
- **Aflatoxin:** untested. Test before selling for feed or food.
- **Moisture:** not entered. Hulls are typically delivered at 88–91% dry matter [wcngg2022].
- **Bioenergy and compost:** both are experimental and need a willing facility, composter, or grower nearby.

## Assumptions and sources

**Sourced:** the haul rate of $0.30 per ton-mile, the recent dairy feed price range of $76–106 per ton, the feed standard, and the local dairy's processing cost.

**Placeholder:** every outlet's final result depends on placeholder values. These include all distances, the bioenergy, compost, distant dairy, and food prices, cleaning costs, and recovered kernel value. Treat the rankings as a demonstration, not a forecast.

Sources:
- [abc_food2025] Almond Board of California, "Unlocking New Value: Commercializing Almond Hulls as Food Ingredients" — https://www.almonds.org/almond-industry/industry-news/unlocking-new-value-commercializing-almond-hulls-food-ingredients

- [gras2026] AgInfo, "Unlocking New Uses for Almond Hulls" — https://www.aginfo.net/report/65481/32/Unlocking-New-Uses-for-Almond-Hulls
- [wcngg2022] WCNGG, "Almond Hull Prices are a Bright Spot" (2022) — https://wcngg.com/2022/04/18/almond-hull-prices-are-a-bright-spot-for-the-almond-industry/

- **Dairy price swings.** Prices have gone from about $60 per ton in a slump to $130 in recent years [farmprogress_low, wcngg2022]. About 97% of hulls go to dairy rations, so buyers have leverage [farmprogress_low]. This moves the cleaning option and the plain dairy sale together.
- **Alternative buyers.** To beat the local dairy, compost would need about $102 per ton, bioenergy $115, and a distant dairy $229. Those are comparison prices, not cost-covering prices.

## Quality and risk checks

- **Aflatoxin: not tested.** Every feed and food route carries this warning. Test before selling.
- **Crude fiber and moisture: not entered.** The CDFA feed standard is crude fiber below 15% [wcngg2022]. Cleaned hulls must still meet it.
- Cleaning requires access to cleaning and kernel-recovery equipment or a toll-cleaning service.
- The local dairy route is established. The cleaning route is emerging.

## Assumptions and sources

**Sourced:** the dairy hull price range of $76–106 per ton, the price history, the feed standard, and the dairy share of hull sales.

**User-entered:** the haul rate of $0.60 per ton-mile.

**Placeholder:** cleaning and processing costs, kernel value, all miles, and every price for compost, bioenergy, distant dairy, and food ingredient. The ranking depends on these placeholders.

scenarios.report:
## Recommendation

Of the six options, "Clean, recover kernels, then sell to local dairy" has the highest expected net: $94 per ton, or about $112,980 for the 1,200-ton lot. That is $8 per ton ($9,060 total) more than selling straight to the local dairy, which nets $87 per ton ($103,920).

The edge is small and rests on user-entered numbers, not sourced ones. The cleaning cost and the value of recovered kernels are both user estimates, and the payload notes the cleaning cost is a demo placeholder. Get a cleaning quote before committing. If the quote is weak, selling to the local dairy is a sound fallback.

## How the options compare

All figures are $ per ton of hulls, after processing and hauling.

| Option | Expected net | vs. local dairy | Price needed to match local dairy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean, recover kernels, sell to local dairy | $94 | +$8 | n/a (price follows dairy) |
| Local dairy (baseline) | $87 | 0 | n/a |
| Distant dairy (240 miles) | $66 | -$21 | $159 |
| Hull powder food ingredient | $53 | -$34 | $184 |
| Compost or soil amendment | $17 | -$70 | $98 |
| Bioenergy feedstock | $14 | -$73 | $105 |

"Price needed to match local dairy" is the price a buyer would have to pay for that option to equal selling locally. It is not a cost-covering price.

The distant dairy's $138 price is eaten by $72 per ton of freight. The food ingredient's $150 price is offset by $70 per ton of processing plus hauling.

## What could change the answer

- **Local dairy price.** The clean-and-recover option sells to the same dairy, so a price change moves both equally. Its edge comes only from its own costs and kernel value.
- **Kernel value.** Recovered kernels are worth $17 to $22 per ton in the estimate, which is the whole advantage. Recovered kernels may grade lower than standard kernels. Processing costs $12 per ton.
- **Food ingredient price.** It would need about $184 per ton to match the local dairy. It has no public market price [gras2026], so only a real buyer quote can settle this.
- **Distant dairy.** It would need about $159 per ton. Rail shipments to Texas have precedent, but the premium is not guaranteed [farmprogress_low].

## Quality and risk checks

- Aflatoxin has been tested. Moisture and crude fiber were not entered, so they are unchecked.
- Feed outlets require crude fiber below 15% [wcngg2022]. Test it before selling to any dairy, and again after cleaning.
- Dairy prices swing widely, from a slump near $60 per ton to $130 [farmprogress_low, wcngg2022]. About 97% of hulls already go to dairy rations, so buyers have leverage [farmprogress_low].
- All six options passed eligibility and have prices, so none needed a quote to be ranked.
- Compost and bioenergy values are demo placeholders.

## Assumptions and sources

- **Sourced:** the haul rate of $0.30 per ton-mile, and the dairy processing cost.
- **User-entered:** all prices, miles, most processing costs, and the recovered kernel value. The payload says placeholders do not affect the results, but the user-entered inputs still need checking against real quotes.
- **Placeholders:** compost and bioenergy values, and the cleaning cost (per the risk note).

Sources:
